executive_summary: The expiration of the Orvan corridor agreement on 10 September 2026 has resulted in a substantial contraction of grain trade value for both Midgard and Tolan. In the fourth quarter of 2026, wheat import values from Orvan fell by approximately USD 156.5M for Midgard and USD 69.6M for Tolan compared to 2025, representing a drop of over 50% in primary sea route value. Midgard's maize imports showed temporary resilience due to delayed delivery terms but eventually collapsed to a USD 126.4M quarterly loss. While alternative supplies from Vanir and rail routes through Ravik have partially mitigated these losses, they are described as smaller, more expensive, and insufficient to bridge the total trade gap.

thor.metric_definition: Aggregate year-on-year change in import value from Orvan for Oct-Dec 2026 compared to Oct-Dec 2025.
assumptions: The three-month window captures the shift from delayed delivery support to the full impact of the corridor's end.
thor.uncertainty_note: Data for Tolan maize is missing, so this estimate is restricted to Midgard.

loki.metric_definition: The year-over-year change in Orvan maize import value for Oct-Dec 2026 versus Oct-Dec 2025.
assumptions: Year-over-year comparison accounts for seasonal variance in maize trade.
missing_data: Maize inventory levels in Midgard as of January 2027.
loki.uncertainty_note: [code: bounds -126.4..-126.4 written as negative changes; taken as magnitudes 126.4..126.4] The 'low' exposure is supported by the delayed volume in October which was nearly 75% of the prior year's level.

odin.metric_definition: Aggregate year-on-year change in import value from Orvan for Oct-Dec 2026 vs Oct-Dec 2025.
assumptions: Initial resilience in October buffered the impact, but the full loss was felt by December.
odin.uncertainty_note: The quarterly loss is well-documented by Tier 1 data and verified by calculation.

thor.metric_definition: Aggregate year-on-year change in import value from Orvan for the months of October, November, and December following the corridor expiry.
assumptions: Aggregate loss across the first full quarter post-expiry is the most robust measure of initial disruption impact.
missing_data: Precise USD value of Vanir wheat substitutes for Midgard in Q4 2026.
thor.uncertainty_note: The high bound equals the low bound as it uses the same three-month aggregate calculation.

loki.metric_definition: The year-over-year change in import value from Orvan for the first full quarter after the agreement expiration (Oct-Dec), representing the gross trade gap.
assumptions: The gross import gap is the primary driver of exposure before accounting for higher-priced substitutes.
missing_data: Precise January 2027 delivery figures from Vanir to confirm the low-end estimate.
loki.uncertainty_note: [code: bounds -156.5..-156.5 written as negative changes; taken as magnitudes 156.5..156.5] The estimate reflects the gross value gap; net exposure is lower due to documented Vanir increases.

odin.metric_definition: Aggregate year-on-year change in import value from Orvan for Oct-Dec 2026 vs Oct-Dec 2025.
assumptions: The Orvan trade gap represents the primary exposure before accounting for partial offsets from more expensive substitutes.
odin.uncertainty_note: Both advocates utilize the same calculated gross loss of USD 156.5M for the Orvan route. While mitigation exists, no aggregate quarterly calculation for the net offset was provided.

outlook.text: The trade disruption is expected to persist through Q1 2027 as importers remain dependent on alternative logistics. Higher costs associated with rail transport and small-parcel sea shipments from Vanir will likely maintain upward pressure on import prices despite partial volume recovery.
assumptions: Corridor agreement remains inactive.
Rail capacity through Ravik remains stable at high usage levels.
Alternative supply from Vanir remains available but priced at a premium.
